title: Lior and the Archive
premise: Wendell Underhill, a clone created to settle the original's estate, arrives at Meridian Colony to find it dying quietly—its people leaving, its records rotting, and its Archive holding the only evidence of who murdered the man whose face he wears. When gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds, Wendell discovers the flicker was a distress pulse from the relay at the edge of dead space, and the Archive itself has begun transmitting his memories to an unknown receiver. Racing across the colony's abandoned infrastructure with archivist Sefa Oyelaran, he learns the original was killed because he found proof that Meridian's collapse was engineered by the corporation that owns them all. At the relay, Wendell must choose between destroying the transmission and preserving the truth: he sends it, claiming the dead man's name not as inheritance but as testimony, and stays behind as the colony's last witness.
about_author: Edmund Pemberton is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical histories of decommissioned space stations. He lives in coastal Maine, where he keeps an archive of obsolete maps and insists memory is a form of engineering.

chapters.title: The Inheritance of Dust
chapters.summary: Wendell arrives at Meridian Colony by slow freighter, carrying legal documents that make him the original Underhill's executor—and his clone. The colony is half-empty, its streets lit by failing solar arrays. His POV establishes quiet dread as residents stare at his borrowed face. Emotional beat: alienation; he belongs nowhere, not even to himself.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: In the colony archive basement, Wendell meets Sefa Oyelaran while cataloguing the original's sealed personal files. Without warning, gravity fails across the entire system for exactly nine seconds—tools float, dust hangs like stars. Wendell's POV captures terror and strange beauty. Emotional beat: wonder cracking open his bureaucratic detachment.

chapters.title: What the Relay Heard
chapters.summary: Sefa traces the nine-second event to a gravitational anomaly originating at the deep-space relay beyond dead space—a station officially decommissioned decades ago. Something there is still broadcasting. Wendell's POV shifts from investigator to believer. Emotional beat: the thrill of a mystery that makes his inherited life feel chosen rather than assigned.

chapters.title: The Original's Last Week
chapters.summary: Decrypted Archive files reveal the original Underhill spent his final week documenting corporate shipments that never arrived and personnel who vanished. He suspected Meridian's decline was deliberate. Wendell reads his own handwriting in another man's journal. Emotional beat: uncanny intimacy—the dead man becomes a brother, then a warning.

chapters.title: Company Men
chapters.summary: A corporate liaison, Ives Corrigan, arrives on the next freighter, ostensibly to assist the estate settlement. His questions about the gravity event are too precise. Wendell plays the obedient clone while hiding the decrypted files. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening; Wendell realizes his existence may be part of someone's cleanup plan.

chapters.title: Dead Space Crossing
chapters.summary: Wendell and Sefa steal a maintenance skiff and cross the dead zone where navigation fails and comms return only static. Sefa confesses she stayed in Meridian because forgetting the colony felt like a second murder. Wendell's POV. Emotional beat: two rootless people choosing each other mid-flight.

chapters.title: The Station That Remembers
chapters.summary: They reach the relay and find it crewed by descendants of workers the corporation erased from every record—living proof of what the Archive holds. The nine-second pulse was their beacon, sent because their life support is failing. Wendell's POV. Emotional beat: grief transformed into solidarity; belonging found among the forgotten.

chapters.title: Signal and Sabotage
chapters.summary: Corrigan's ship arrives armed; the corporation intends to erase the relay and everyone aboard. Wendell discovers the Archive uplink can broadcast the full record system-wide—but only if someone stays to hold the connection manually through the assault. Sefa volunteers. Wendell refuses to let her die for his name. Emotional beat: sacrifice confronted head-on.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Climax. As Corrigan's forces board, Wendell initiates the broadcast, narrating the original's evidence in his own voice—clone and original speaking as one. The truth floods every colony channel; Meridian's remaining residents rise, and corporate ships withdraw under public exposure. Wendell nearly dies holding the console. Emotional beat: fury and release; inheritance claimed as action.

chapters.title: The Slow Return of Gravity
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Meridian rebuilds around its reopened Archive. Wendell signs documents as 'Wendell Underhill' and means himself, no one else. Sefa returns from the relay alive; the forgotten crews come home. He begins recording the colony's history—not a case file, but a chronicle. Emotional beat: peace earned; memory and belonging finally his own.
